LLY-2026-10-02: When did the FDA approve Jaypirca for first-line CLL?

The FDA approved pirtobrutinib (Jaypirca, Eli Lilly and Company) on October 2, 2026 for adult patients with previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) with no known 17p deletion, per the FDA's approval notification of that date.

The FDA first approved Jaypirca on January 27, 2023, under accelerated approval for relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least two lines of systemic therapy including a BTK inhibitor. It added CLL/SLL after at least two prior lines of therapy including a BTK inhibitor and a BCL-2 inhibitor on December 1, 2023 (accelerated approval), granted traditional approval for adults with relapsed or refractory CLL/SLL previously treated with a covalent BTK inhibitor on December 3, 2025, and approved first-line use in CLL/SLL with no known 17p deletion on October 2, 2026.
What trial supported the Jaypirca first-line CLL approval?

BRUIN CLL-313 (NCT05023980), a randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial in 282 patients with previously untreated CLL or SLL without deletion of chromosome 17p, comparing pirtobrutinib with bendamustine plus a rituximab product. Progression-free survival assessed by an independent review committee had a hazard ratio of 0.20 (95% CI 0.11 to 0.37; p<0.0001), per the FDA.
What is the approved Jaypirca dose for CLL?

The FDA's notification gives the recommended pirtobrutinib dose as 200 mg orally once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The FDA says full prescribing information will be posted on Drugs@FDA; Lilly's announcement links the current prescribing information.
RHHBY-2026-10-08: When did the FDA approve Tecentriq for Stage III colon cancer?

The FDA approved atezolizumab (Tecentriq, Genentech) on October 8, 2026, in combination with a fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin, for the adjuvant treatment of adult and pediatric patients two years of age and older with Stage III mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) colon cancer, per the FDA's approval notification of that date. Genentech had given October 9, 2026 as the goal date, so the action came one day early.
What trial supported the Tecentriq colon cancer approval?

ATOMIC/ML39057 (NCT02912559), a randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial in 711 adults and one pediatric patient with resected Stage III dMMR colon cancer, comparing atezolizumab plus mFOLFOX6 then atezolizumab alone with mFOLFOX6 alone. The disease-free survival hazard ratio was 0.50 (95% CI 0.35 to 0.73; p 0.0001), per the FDA.
Was Tecentriq Hybreza also approved for colon cancer?

Yes. The same FDA notification approved atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs (Tecentriq Hybreza) with a fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin for the adjuvant treatment of patients 12 years and older who weigh 40 kg or more with Stage III dMMR colon cancer.
What is the recommended Tecentriq dose for Stage III colon cancer?

For adults the FDA gives 840 mg every two weeks, 1200 mg every three weeks or 1680 mg every four weeks intravenously with chemotherapy for six months, then atezolizumab alone for six months or until disease recurrence or unacceptable toxicity. The FDA says full prescribing information will be posted on Drugs@FDA.
NVS-2026-10-06: When did the FDA approve Rhapsido for symptomatic dermographism?

The FDA's Drugs@FDA data record the approval of the Rhapsido (remibrutinib) efficacy supplement, NDA 218436 supplement 1, on October 6, 2026. Novartis announced it on October 7, 2026, for adults with symptomatic dermographism inadequately controlled by H1 antihistamines.
What trial supported the Rhapsido symptomatic dermographism approval?
The symptomatic dermographism cohort of the Phase III RemIND trial. Per Novartis, 29.3% of patients on Rhapsido achieved a complete response from hives at Week 12 versus 14.0% on placebo (p=0.0229).
The FDA first approved Rhapsido (remibrutinib) on September 30, 2025, for adults with chronic spontaneous urticaria inadequately controlled by H1 antihistamines (NDA 218436).
IBRX-2026-10-14: When did the FDA approve Anktiva for papillary-only bladder cancer?

The FDA approved nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln (Anktiva, ImmunityBio) with BCG on October 14, 2026 for adults with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer, expanding the indication to include high-grade papillary-only tumors, per the FDA's approval notification of that date. ImmunityBio had given January 6, 2027 as the goal date, so the action came 84 days early.
What evidence supported the Anktiva papillary-only approval?

Per the FDA, efficacy was previously shown in Cohort A of QUILT-3.032 (NCT03022825), 77 patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with carcinoma in situ, with a complete response rate of 62% (95% CI 51 to 73). The FDA extended that result to high-grade papillary-only disease on review of the available scientific information, citing the overlapping clinical features of the two tumor types.
RHHBY-2026-10-15: Was Enspryng approved for thyroid eye disease?

Yes. Drugs@FDA records the approval letter for BLA 761149 supplement 8 dated October 15, 2026, the goal date. Genentech announced it the same day and describes Enspryng as the first and only at-home subcutaneous treatment for TED.
What trials supported the Enspryng TED approval?

The Phase III SatraGO-1 and SatraGO-2 studies, 258 patients in total. Per Genentech, SatraGO-1 did not meet its primary endpoint at week 24, while SatraGO-2 showed a proptosis response of 52.9% with Enspryng versus 23.4% on placebo and diplopia reduction of 60.7% versus 25.8% in patients with active TED.
Does Enspryng have another FDA decision pending?
Yes. Genentech says the FDA is expected to decide on Enspryng for MOGAD (myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease) by January 10, 2027, under priority review.
IRD-2026-10-16: Who sells RYZUMVI for presbyopia in the U.S.?

Per Opus Genetics, Viatris holds exclusive rights to commercialize phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% in the United States under a global licensing agreement, and the approval triggers a milestone payment to Opus.
What trials supported the presbyopia approval?
The Phase 3 VEGA-2 and VEGA-3 trials, both of which met their primary and all key secondary efficacy endpoints with no treatment-related serious adverse events reported, according to Opus Genetics.

GSK-2026-10-19: Was Jemperli approved for locally advanced rectal cancer?

Yes. The FDA granted accelerated approval on October 19, 2026 to dostarlimab-gxly (Jemperli) for adults with Stage II/III locally advanced rectal cancer that is mismatch repair deficient or microsatellite instability high, per the FDA's own notification. GSK announced it the same day. Continued approval may depend on a confirmatory trial.
Was the Jemperli rectal cancer decision early?

The FDA acted on October 19, 2026. GSK's August 24, 2026 release stated the goal date as February 2027, a month rather than a day, so pdufa.bio does not publish an early or late margin for this decision. GSK's release says the approval came ahead of the PDUFA date; the application carried Priority Review and a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher.

Per the FDA, AZUR-1 (NCT05723562) enrolled 154 previously untreated patients who received dostarlimab alone for nine cycles. Sustained clinical complete response at 12 months was 47% by independent central review in 116 evaluable patients and 68% by investigator assessment in 144; overall response by central review was 79%. With a median follow-up of 26.3 months, no patient with a complete or near-complete response had progressed.
GSK-2026-10-20: Yes. The FDA approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) on October 20, 2026, per the FDA's own press announcement of that day, for chronic hepatitis B in combination with existing antiviral therapy in certain adults without cirrhosis. GSK announced it the same day. It is the first antisense oligonucleotide approved for hepatitis B.
Yes, by 6 days. The goal date was October 26, 2026 (Ionis's 8-K of July 29, 2026, under Priority Review) and the FDA's announcement is dated October 20, 2026.
What did the B-Well trials show?

Per the FDA, across the two placebo-controlled trials 24% of patients on Hibsago met the criteria to stop their existing hepatitis B therapy versus none on placebo, and 19% still had the virus under control with undetectable HBsAg 24 weeks after stopping all treatment. Hibsago carries a boxed warning for serious liver reactions and low platelet counts.
GSK-2026-11-17: Was neladalkib approved by the FDA?

Yes. The FDA granted accelerated approval on November 17, 2026 to neladalkib (Nelkarmi) for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer previously treated with alectinib as the only ALK inhibitor, or with two or more ALK inhibitors and platinum-based chemotherapy, per the FDA's own notification. GSK announced it the same day. Continued approval may depend on a confirmatory trial.

Yes, by 10 days. The FDA acted on November 17, 2026; the goal date was November 27, 2026, as stated by Nuvalent when the application was accepted with Priority Review (May 27, 2026). GSK's release also says the approval came ahead of the original target action date.

Per the FDA, confirmed overall response by blinded independent central review was 49% in 67 patients whose only prior ALK inhibitor was alectinib and 32% in 155 patients after two or more ALK inhibitors and platinum-based chemotherapy. Among responders, 52% and 51% respectively had responses lasting at least 12 months.
REGN-2026-11-18: Was cemdisiran approved by the FDA?

Yes. Regeneron announced on November 18, 2026 that the FDA approved Livsayis (cemdisiran) for adults with generalized myasthenia gravis who are anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive. The FDA's own record of the action day had not been posted when this page was published.

pdufa.bio does not publish a margin for this decision. Regeneron stated the target action date as November 2026, a month rather than a day, after using a Priority Review Voucher, and the approval was announced on November 18, 2026, within that month.
What did the NIMBLE trial show?

Per Regeneron, at week 24 the MG-ADL score improved 4.5 points with Livsayis versus 2.2 with placebo, and 76.6% of patients versus 44.1% on placebo had at least a 3-point improvement. Livsayis is given under the skin four times a year and carries a boxed warning for serious meningococcal infections.
SNY-2026-11-18: Was venglustat approved by the FDA?

Yes. On November 18, 2026 the FDA approved Infilbray (venglustat) tablets for the neurological symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher disease in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kg, per the FDA's own news release. The FDA calls it the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher disease. The approval was granted to Genzyme Corporation, a Sanofi company.
What study supported the Infilbray approval?

Per the FDA, a randomized, double-blind study of 43 patients aged 12 and older with Type 3 Gaucher disease who had been stabilized on enzyme replacement therapy. Patients took Infilbray once daily by mouth or continued intravenous enzyme replacement therapy every two weeks for 52 weeks; at Week 52 the Infilbray group improved on a measure combining ataxia and cognitive assessments compared with the enzyme replacement therapy group.
Did venglustat have a PDUFA date?
We hold no publicly disclosed goal date for it, so it was not a dated event on our calendar. The FDA's release says the application had Priority Review and Orphan Drug designation.
JNJ-2026-11-05: Was RYBREVANT FASPRO approved for head and neck cancer?

Yes. The FDA granted accelerated approval on November 5, 2026, per its own approval letter, for adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma whose disease progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and an anti-PD-(L)1 antibody. It is not indicated for HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
AZN-2026-11-13: What did the FDA approve for Imfinzi on November 13, 2026?

Per Drugs@FDA and AstraZeneca, Imfinzi (durvalumab) with enfortumab vedotin-ejfv before radical cystectomy, followed by Imfinzi alone after surgery, for adults with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who are ineligible for or have refused cisplatin-based chemotherapy.
NVS-2026-11-16: Is Cosentyx approved for polymyalgia rheumatica?

Yes. The FDA's approval letter, signed November 16, 2026, adds polymyalgia rheumatica in adults as a new indication for Cosentyx (secukinumab). Novartis says the approval covers 150 mg for patients who had an inadequate response to corticosteroids or cannot tolerate a corticosteroid taper.
PFE-2026-10-26: Was Talzenna with Xtandi approved for castration-sensitive prostate cancer?

Yes. The FDA approved talazoparib (Talzenna) with enzalutamide on October 26, 2026 for adults with metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naive or -sensitive prostate cancer with HRR gene mutations detected by an FDA-authorized test, per the FDA's own notification. Pfizer announced it the same day.
Was the Talzenna TALAPRO-3 decision early?

Pfizer's July 22, 2026 release gave the PDUFA action date only as the last quarter of 2026, so pdufa.bio does not publish an early or late margin. The FDA acted on October 26, 2026, inside that quarter.

Per the FDA, among 599 patients with HRR gene-mutated disease, adding talazoparib to enzalutamide cut the risk of radiographic progression or death (hazard ratio 0.48, 95% CI 0.36 to 0.65); median radiographic progression-free survival was not reached versus 45.8 months with placebo.
CAPR-2026-11-20: Was deramiocel approved by the FDA?

No. Capricor announced on November 20, 2026 that the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter on its resubmitted BLA for deramiocel in Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Per Capricor, the FDA does not consider the data sufficient to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness and cites certain other clinical deficiencies.
Was the deramiocel decision before the PDUFA date?

Yes, by 2 days. The FDA's own Complete Response Letter is dated November 20, 2026, and the goal date was November 22, 2026. Capricor announced the letter that evening at 7:55 PM ET, after the market close.
Is this the first CRL for deramiocel?
No. Capricor announced an earlier Complete Response Letter for deramiocel on July 11, 2025, and then resubmitted the application.
AZN-2026-11-16: Is gefurulimab approved by the FDA?

Yes. The FDA approved Klygefa (gefurulimab-gaks) on November 13, 2026 for adults with generalized myasthenia gravis who are anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody positive (BLA 761488). AstraZeneca announced it on November 16, 2026.
Per AstraZeneca, Klygefa is self-administered under the skin once a week with an autoinjector. The FDA letter approves a REMS because of the risk of serious meningococcal infections.
Was the Klygefa decision early or late?
pdufa.bio holds no publicly disclosed PDUFA goal date for this application, so no margin is given. The FDA letter states that the application was received on November 13, 2025.
BBIO-2026-11-23: Was BBP-418 (ribitol) approved by the FDA?

Yes. BridgeBio announced on November 23, 2026 that the FDA granted traditional (full) approval to Welgemda (BBP-418, ribitol) for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 in adult and pediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg.

BridgeBio announced the approval on November 23, 2026, four days before the November 27, 2026 PDUFA goal date it had disclosed. pdufa.bio publishes a margin only from the FDA's own record of the action day, which had not been read when this page was published.
What did the FORTIFY trial show?
Per BridgeBio, at 12 months the 100-meter timed test showed a 0.27 m/s velocity benefit relative to placebo (p<0.0001), and forced vital capacity (percent predicted) a 4.89% benefit (p=0.0071).
COGT-2026-11-24: Was bezuclastinib approved by the FDA?

Yes. The FDA approved bezuclastinib (Ekitna) on November 24, 2026, in combination with sunitinib, for adults with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors who have received prior treatment with imatinib, per the FDA's own notification.
Yes, by 6 days. The FDA acted on November 24, 2026; the goal date was November 30, 2026, as stated by Cogent in its 8-K of August 10, 2026.
Does this approval cover systemic mastocytosis?

No. The FDA notice names only GIST with sunitinib. Cogent's applications in nonadvanced systemic mastocytosis (goal date December 30, 2026) and advanced systemic mastocytosis (goal date June 29, 2027) are tracked separately and remain open.
What did the PEAK trial show?

Per the FDA, in 413 patients median progression-free survival was 16.5 months with bezuclastinib plus sunitinib and 9.2 months with sunitinib alone (hazard ratio 0.50). Overall survival data were not mature.
RHHBY-2026-11-23: Was giredestrant approved for early breast cancer?

Yes. The FDA approved giredestrant (Wilserdly) on November 23, 2026 as a single agent for the adjuvant treatment of adults with ER-positive, HER2-negative, stage I, II and III breast cancer at intermediate to high risk of recurrence, per the FDA's own notification. Genentech announced it the same day.
Was the adjuvant Wilserdly decision early?
Yes, by 7 days. The FDA acted on November 23, 2026; Genentech had said on June 1, 2026 that the FDA was expected to decide by November 30, 2026.
Is this the same approval as Wilserdly with everolimus?
No. The FDA approved Wilserdly with everolimus for ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer on November 16, 2026. The November 23 approval is the separate adjuvant use, on the lidERA trial.
PYPD-2026-11-24: Was D-PLEX100 approved by the FDA?

Yes. PolyPid announced on November 24, 2026 that the FDA approved its NDA for BACFENSSI (doxycycline hyclate), previously known as D-PLEX100, to reduce the occurrence of surgical site infections in adults and pediatric patients weighing 45 kg or more undergoing colorectal surgery with incisions longer than 20 cm.

PolyPid announced the approval on November 24, 2026, four days before the November 28, 2026 goal date it had disclosed. pdufa.bio publishes a margin only from the FDA's own record of the action day, which had not been read when this page was published.
